page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores running at 4.2 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a massive 480 MB L3 cache, 16.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core), and a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded capabilities, with gzip compression reaching top-tier speeds of 36.47 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression scoring a strong 15.05 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4653.8 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 29.54 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is mixed, with large-block read-only operations averaging 43.94 GB/sec, while small-block cached reads and large-block writes fall into the lower performance tier. Passmark CPU, memory, and database operations consistently rank in the average tier.

This server represents a balanced general-purpose hardware profile, offering dedicated compute resources and fast local NVMe storage without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-core scaling and write bandwidth compared to its single-core efficiency. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, redis caching, lightweight database operations, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
